title: Capacity fuzzy hedging and error-bank playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
=======
This playbook defines the 'fuzzy hedging' approach to capacity and a complementary operational pattern we call the Error Bank: a short-term, auditable tokenized buffer that lets teams absorb transient SLO consumption spikes without immediate full-capacity commitments. The goal is to improve customer-facing reliability while minimizing costly overprovisioning and preserving clear recovery paths.

Key outcomes:
- Reduce unnecessary reserved capacity spend by 10–35% for bursty tenants.
- Keep P99 latency SLOs intact for customer-critical tiers during short-term load spikes.
- Provide rapid, low-friction mitigation options for oncall with clear revert criteria.

When to use this playbook
------------------------
- For multi-tenant inference services with bursty or seasonal traffic (embedding jobs, batch reranking, real-time spikes).
- When rapid headroom provisioning takes >10 minutes or carries a significant cost commitment.
- As an intermediate mitigation layer between autoscaling and tenant throttling/eviction.

Core concepts
-------------
1) Fuzzy hedging (probabilistic headroom allocation)
- Use probabilistic forecasts (mix of short-term EWMA and calendar-aware ML model) to allocate ephemeral headroom instead of hard slot reservations.
- Hedge factor (H) is defined per-tenant-class: H = quantile(forecast, q) * safety_multiplier. Typical defaults: q=0.90 for standard tenants, q=0.98 for enterprise-critical. safety_multiplier in [1.05, 1.20].

2) Error Bank (tokenized short-term error-credit)
- Error Bank is a per-tenant credit account expressed in SLO-seconds (e.g., latency or error budget units) that can be consumed automatically under controlled conditions.
- Bank top-ups are policy-driven (manual, scheduled, or earned via low-burn windows).

3) Tiered fallback policy
- Tier 0 (critical): allocate hedged headroom and emergency Error Bank top-up; do not throttle.
- Tier 1 (standard): allow Error Bank consumption and progressive request shaping.
- Tier 2 (best-effort): aggressive shedding and pre-approved eviction path.

Telemetry & signals (required)
-----------------------------
Below table lists minimum telemetry and alert thresholds for using fuzzy hedging + Error Bank. All signals must be available to the SRE capacity orchestrator pipeline.

| Metric name | Source | Window | Alert threshold | Notes |
|-------------|--------|--------|-----------------|-------|
| p50/p95/p99 latency | request_traces | 1m/5m/1h | p99 > target * 1.2 | target = SLO 99th latency |
| SLO burn rate | slo_pipeline | 1m | burn_rate > 4x baseline | triggers bank check |
| headroom utilization | autoscaler | 1m | hedged_headroom_used > 70% | implies additional hedging needed |
| queue depth | inference_queue | 30s | depth > 100 and growth rate > 20%/min | triggers burst mitigation |
| error-bank balance | capacity_orchestrator | 1m | balance < 20% | preflight to replenish |

Operational patterns (step-by-step)
----------------------------------
1) Preflight (daily / before major launch)
  1.1 Run 'forecast-check' in the capacity lab for the tenant group: 
      - CLI: rwd-capacity forecast-check --tenant-group <name> --horizon 6h --baseline 2w
  1.2 Validate telemetry freshness and signal mapping (use the table above).
  1.3 Confirm Error Bank policy attached to tenant (see Policy matrix).

2) Normal operation (automated)
  2.1 Orchestrator produces hedged headroom recommendations every 60s.
  2.2 If SLO burn_rate < 1.5x baseline, allow normal operation.
  2.3 If burn_rate between 1.5x and 4x, allow Error Bank consumption up to configured cap and send "bank-usage" annotation to oncall.
  2.4 If burn_rate > 4x or bank depleted, progress through Tiered fallback policy.

3) Oncall playbook (human intervention)
  3.1 Pager fires for: p99 latency > target*1.3 for 5m OR bank_balance < 10% AND headroom_used > 80%.
  3.2 Triage checklist:
    - Confirm signal integrity (no telemetry gaps).
    - Identify whether spike matches known schedule (release, campaign).
    - Review forecast vs actual: rwd-capacity compare-forecast --tenant <id>.
  3.3 Rapid mitigations (order matters):
    1) Activate short-lived hedged burst: rwd-capacity bump-headroom --tenant <id> --minutes 15 --reason "oncall-bump"
    2) If failed or headroom not available: enable request shaping policy for tenant  (shape to 80% of steady-state).
    3) If still failing: pre-notify customer success and escalate to Tiered eviction (Tier 2).
  3.4 Post-incident: document bank consumption and rationalize top-up decision in the incident review.

Policy matrix (examples)
----------------------
- Standard tenant: hedging quantile q=0.90, safety_multiplier=1.1, bank cap = 30 SLO-seconds per 1M tokens, auto-replenish disabled.
- Enterprise tier: q=0.98, safety_multiplier=1.05, bank cap = 150 SLO-seconds per 1M tokens, auto-replenish enabled (scheduled low-burn windows allow top-ups).
- Burst-only partner: q=0.85, safety_multiplier=1.2, bank cap = 50 SLO-seconds per burst-window, auto-topup only with manual approval.

Implementation notes (integration points)
----------------------------------------
- Orchestrator service: capacity-orchestrator (k8s svc: capacity-orch.default.svc.cluster.local). Exposes REST endpoints: /forecast, /hedge, /bank.
- Autoscaler hooks: use hook 'preemptive_expand' to apply hedged headroom for short durations.
- Observability: map error-bank and hedging annotations into traces via X-Redwood-Capacity header for downstream correlation.
- Audit trail: all bank transactions are recorded to ledger (postgres table capacity_bank_ledger). Ledger entries must include: tenant_id, amount, reason, operator, tx_id.

YAML example: hedged headroom request
-----------------------------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: HedgedHeadroomRequest
metadata:
  tenant: "acme-analytics"
spec:
  duration_minutes: 20
  quantity_gpu_units: 2
  reason: "scheduled-campaign-surge"

CLI examples
------------
- Check bank balance: rwd-capacity bank-status --tenant acme-analytics
- Force top-up (manual): rwd-capacity bank-topup --tenant acme-analytics --amount 50 --note "postmortem approved"
- Revoke hedged headroom early: rwd-capacity revoke-hedge --tx <tx_id>

Runbook for controlled rehearsal (game day)
------------------------------------------
1) Scope: pick 2 production-like tenants with different profiles (one standard, one enterprise).
2) Inject synthetic traffic to drive p99 to 1.1x SLO for 10 minutes.
3) Observe error-bank deduction behavior and auditor logs.
4) Validate that hedged headroom applied and removed cleanly.
5) Run rollback: simulate rapid bank depletion and confirm Tiered fallback triggers.
6) Document timings and any unexpected manual steps.

Decision criteria and metrics to track
-------------------------------------
Track these metrics weekly for 6 weeks after rollout:
- Reserve spend delta vs baseline (dollars/week). Goal: <= +5% in steady-state, -10% to -35% during burst seasons.
- Frequency of bank-triggered mitigations and average duration.
- Number of manual top-ups per calendar month. Goal: <= 2 for mature tenants.
- Incidents where hedged headroom failed to prevent SLO breach. Goal: 0 for Tier 0; <=1/month for Tier 1 during early rollout.

Ownership & run governance
-------------------------
- Capacity product owner: Priya Kumar (product).
- Implementation and ops: eng-sre -> capacity-orchestrator team (primary oncall).
- Policy approvals: SRE leadership + Revenue Ops for billing/credits.
- Review cadence: quarterly postmortem review of all bank consumption events.

Incident review expectations
--------------------------
- Any incident where Error Bank consumption > 40% of cap or where hedged headroom was applied for > 30 minutes must produce a 1-page incident review within 48 hours (template provided).
- Review must include: root cause hypothesis, telemetry snapshot, forecast mismatch analysis, and a remediation plan with owner and due date.

Open questions & future work
--------------------------
- Explore ML-driven adaptive safety_multiplier that decays after repeated low-burn windows.
- Integrate cost-awareness into the hedging decision (dollars-per-token threshold).
- Extend Error Bank semantics to embedding batch jobs (credits proportional to token-window).

Appendix: quick reference table
------------------------------
| Action | Trigger | Safety check | Operator command | Expected RTO |
|--------|---------|--------------|------------------|--------------|
| Hedged bump | burn_rate > 1.5x and bank available | ledger write success | rwd-capacity bump-headroom | 60–120s |
| Bank top-up (manual) | postmortem approved | billing sign-off | rwd-capacity bank-topup | N/A (manual) |
| Request shaping | headroom not available and burn_rate > 2x | policy gate | rwd-config apply-shaper --tenant | 30–90s |
| Tenant eviction | sustained breach > 20m | exec approval | rwd-ops evict-tenant --tenant | 5–15m |
